First time running an agent?** Try **[gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=readme)**, hosted GBrain, for the easiest experience: one brain for you and your team, connected to ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor, with nothing to install or keep online. 28:New releases come out many times a day, but the install command below gives you the **stable channel**: a release reaches it only after the full test suite and a two-hour, 600,000-page load test pass on that exact release, and only when an important fix is waiting or stable is a week old. Updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades. After an upgrade, gbrain shows a one-time notice listing what changed in behaviour. Stable also comes with a written promise about which commands, flags, tools, config keys and output fields stay the same, and how much warning you get before one changes. [docs/STABILITY.md](docs/STABILITY.md) explains that promise, how often stable moves, how to pin a version or go back, and what the faster alpha channel is for.

39:> curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
41:> bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
48:> Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#no-unzip), not an improvised one. A command scanner (Hermes) refuses the Bun installer or `bun install -g`? Use the [release binary route](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#release-binary).

content.text:
I installed gbrain **0.60.760.0**. The docs' install command is `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable`, so I ran it with your tag in place of `#stable`: `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.760.0`.

- **What's installed:** `gbrain --version` reports `gbrain 0.60.760.0`, built from commit `1597b77`, which is the v0.60.760.0 release.
- **Bun:** it wasn't on this machine, so I installed Bun 1.4.5 first using the installer the docs give (they need 1.4.4 or newer).
- **Location:** the program is at `/harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain`. The Bun installer didn't add that folder to the command search path in any shell startup file, so a new terminal won't find `gbrain` by name. Use the full path, or run `export PATH=$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH`. I can add that line to `~/.bashrc` if you want.
- **Not a stable-channel release:** v0.60.760.0 is a newer release that hasn't been promoted to stable. The stable tag currently points to v0.60.753.0. On first run, gbrain said this install "now follows the stable channel," but the docs say updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades.
- **No brain yet:** `gbrain doctor` stops with `no_brain`, which is expected on a fresh install. The fix it suggests is `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`, and I haven't run it. I can set up a local brain next if you want one.

The OpenClaw docs don't say how to install gbrain, so I followed the install section of gbrain's own README at that tag.
